text:
The Ducks are now winless in five, 0-5-0, and this one slipped away in the first period. New Jersey out-chanced Anaheim 1.52 to 0.18 in expected goals, a measure of the quality of shots taken, before the opening 20 minutes were over. Arseny Gritsyuk tipped in the first goal at 4:38, and Nico Hischier added a power-play tip-in with 41 seconds left in the period to make it 2-0.

Anaheim got back into it in the third. Tim Washe tipped one in at 8:20, with assists from Jackson LaCombe and Sam Colangelo, and it was 2-1. But the Ducks never pulled level. Anthony Mantha answered at 13:27 with a wrist shot, and Jack Hughes sealed it with an empty-looking backhand at 19:53 that closed the scoring at 4-1. The Devils' second-period chances were close to even with Anaheim's (0.71 to 0.76), which is as near as the Ducks came to controlling any stretch.

By the numbers, the result was fair. New Jersey finished with 3.16 expected goals to Anaheim's 1.51, and "deserved to win" (the share of simulated replays of every shot that a team wins) came out 79 percent for the Devils. Nico Daws was steady in goal, stopping 16 of 17 shots, and Jesper Bratt earned first star with two assists. For Anaheim, the search for a win goes on at 0-5-0. The facts here don't include New Jersey's record or streak.
